openings.claim: Does the incumbent bolted-strip/cork clamp have achievable preload satisfying retention and gloved service time together? Keep its carrier; replace assumed screw preload with paired displacement/service measurements at recorded screw settings. No replacement is established.
openings.discriminator: The nearest rival is that retention-sufficient preload makes screwdriver release/return too slow. Low displacement with service above sixty seconds supports it; compliant displacement and service together weaken it. The 3 N versus 7 N magnet-release difference predicts neither cork friction nor clamp performance on the spare.
openings.probe: Before drilling strips, check M4 slot fit, compliant placement and screwdriver access. If possible, fabricate one configuration within eighty minutes using supplied parts. Within twenty observation minutes, perform at most three twenty-stroke runs and three paired removal/return checks; record screw settings, displacement and timing. Use the spare for the final run, thick gloves for its removal, and handle only unmarked regions. Displacement above 1 mm or service above sixty seconds defeats the tested setting. No accessible compliant placement defeats this configuration; exhausted time leaves untested settings unresolved.
openings.uncertainty: Slot dimensions, strip stiffness and screwdriver access must permit assembly. Recorded settings may not reproduce adequate preload after cork compression or plate substitution. Observation time may not permit informative paired checks; neither assembly nor joint performance is established.

lineage.reason: Retains the clamp relation, coupled preload/service rival and complete defeat test, magnet inference limit, resource/stopping caveats, assumptions and declared uncertain fit.

decision: Retain D1 as an unresolved test. Do not drill, cut, heat or glue plate/carriage; expose the marked 30 mm working edge, keep additions outside stroke clearance and carriage attached to rails. Unknown feasibility grants no constraint relaxation. A passing setting supplies bounded probe evidence, not deployment or unspecified-load reliability.
